pattern_set: ident_compare: a TOKEN-based duration identifier (see duration_as_proof_scan._is_duration_identifier) compared to a zero literal. The unit word (ms/msec/millis/milliseconds/seconds/secs/sec/duration/elapsed/micros/nanos, plus us/ns as a whole underscore segment only) may be the whole identifier, a suffix (Ms/Seconds/_ms), or an earlier word followed by a qualifier (wallMsDelta, expectedDurationSeconds) -- position-independent by design.

duration_getter: a niladic call `fooBar()` whose name is itself a duration identifier by the same rule (e.g. getFooMilliseconds()), compared to a zero literal. Formerly named 'milliseconds_getter' and limited to the literal suffix 'Milliseconds'.
json_ms_key: a QJsonObject '*_ms' key read via .toDouble()/.toInt(), WITH OR WITHOUT a default-value argument (e.g. .toDouble(-1.0)), compared to a zero literal.

assert_macro: a gtest predicate macro encoding a duration-vs-zero comparison -- 2-arg ASSERT_*/EXPECT_* (EQ NE GT GE LT LE DOUBLE_EQ FLOAT_EQ) whose two arguments are a zero literal and a duration expression, or 3-arg ASSERT_NEAR/EXPECT_NEAR(val1, val2, abs_error) applying the same check to (val1, val2) and ignoring the tolerance.
_meta.round_4b_grammar_hardening: Round 4B (successor of the parked #173 review) replaced round 4's four literal-suffix/fixed-macro-list patterns with the token-based rule above after sol and fable independently found real, then-current false negatives (camelCase Seconds/Duration names with no _ms/_seconds/Ms suffix, a bare 'ms' identifier, .toDouble() with a default argument, and ASSERT_NEAR/ASSERT_DOUBLE_EQ outside the macro allow-list). The rule is deliberately still bounded, not maximal: 'us'/'ns' only count as a whole underscore-delimited segment (never a bare camelCase Us/Ns token, too collision-prone), and shapes with zero live instances in this tree at round-4B time (qFuzzyIsNull, std::max(0.0, x_ms), a bare *Seconds() getter, chrono .count() compares) were deliberately left unmatched -- broadening for a shape nothing here uses would only add false-positive surface with no coverage benefit. The scanner also now blanks `//` and `/* */` comment text (tracking multi-line block comments and string literals) before matching, since the broader identifier rule turned two comments describing duration behavior in prose into false positives under the old raw-text scan. Anchors are computed by a small tokenizer (identifiers/numbers/operators/punctuation, single-space-joined, string literals kept as one verbatim atom) instead of a whitespace-collapse, so token-boundary spacing choices (`if(x)` vs `if ( x )`) no longer change a site's identity while whitespace INSIDE a string literal still does; this changed nearly every existing anchor's exact text in this round's migration (a mechanical resync, verified against the previous rows by shared line numbers -- no row's classification changed, only its anchor/lines fields). A site's identity also now includes its occurrence COUNT (see test_duration_as_proof_inventory._row_key), not just (path, anchor), so a newly added identical copy of an already-classified line cannot silently inherit that row's verdict.
_meta.lower_bound_caveat: This inventory is a LOWER BOUND on 'duration used as run-proof' sites, not a completeness proof. The scanner (tools/repo_hygiene/duration_as_proof_scan.py) only matches the four textual shapes above, per physical line (a comparison split across two physical lines is not caught), over git-tracked *.c/*.cpp/*.h/*.hpp files under src/, platform/qt/ and tests/. A duration compared through an intermediate variable on another line, a helper function that hides the comparison, a duration hidden inside a multi-line block comment's own multi-line reach, or a fifth pattern shape entirely, would not be caught. The gate's job is to make the class it DOES see finite and reviewed, not to prove no other duration-as-proof site exists anywhere in the codebase.

classes.division_guard: Guards a division (X / duration) against a zero denominator; the comparison exists to avoid a divide-by-zero/NaN, never to prove a stage ran.
classes.display_or_format: Formats or converts an already-computed duration for display or logging (unit conversion, an FPS-equivalent for a print); the zero-guard only avoids a garbage displayed value.
classes.value_fallback_select: Selects between a measured value and a fallback/default, or filters a sample/sentinel before recording it, based on whether a duration read as zero/non-positive; a config or data-validity decision, not a run-proof.
classes.not_run_proof_structural: A structural check that can never distinguish 'ran' from 'did not run' (e.g. >=0.0 non-negativity), or a negative-lane exclusivity check proving a stage did NOT run (paired elsewhere with a positive completed-flag/counter proof that another stage DID).
classes.run_proof: Duration-as-proof in the sense this card exists to retire: a zero/nonzero duration read is the ONLY signal that a stage ran, produced output, or is exclusive of another stage, with no completed-flag/counter alternative recorded alongside it. Carries either a 'flag' naming an already-existing replacement, or 'status: open' + 'successor' naming the card that will fix it.

clocks.qpc_stage_clock: mlv_stage_timing_now()/_ns() (src/debug/StageTiming.h) or another QueryPerformanceCounter-based monotonic clock (e.g. GpuWindowSwapTelemetry's *QpcMs fields); falls back to omp_get_wtime() only if QueryPerformanceFrequency itself fails, so not a flake source in practice.
clocks.omp_get_wtime_direct: Calls omp_get_wtime() unconditionally with no monotonic-clock fallback (raw_processing.c's per-substage Shadows/Highlights filter timers, ~1484-1694); the #169 ruling's correction names this family as the ONLY source of the 1 ms flake.
clocks.other: A config value, CLI argument, epoch/wall-clock sentinel, Qt QTime delta, std::chrono::steady_clock read, or a field whose clock was not independently traced this round; not itself a flake-risk clock in the omp_get_wtime sense.

rows.justification: Guards the fps = (swapCount-1)*1000/spanMs division; with <=1 swap or a zero-width span (QPC ties) the guard reports 0 rather than dividing by zero. Decides a formatting fallback for an already-computed summary, never whether any stage ran.

Guards normalizedProcessCpuPercent()'s cpuSecondsDelta / (wallMsDelta/1000.0) division: a negative CPU delta (clock read failure, sentinel -1.0 propagated) or a non-positive wall-time sample span returns -1.0 (unavailable) instead of dividing. Formatting/availability guard for a CPU% diagnostic, never a stage run-proof.

Selects between a caller-supplied measured average frame time and a synthetic 120%-over-budget estimate when constructing a forced-fast playback-quality decision for test/diagnostic callers; does not gate whether any pipeline stage executed.

MLVAPP_AUTOPLAY_SECONDS is an automation/test env-var config flag: >0 enables the auto-play-then-stop hook, 0 (unset) leaves it off. A feature-enablement config decision, not proof that any pipeline stage ran.
MLVAPP_AUTOPLAY_SETTLE_MS is an operator-supplied config knob (ms to wait before autoplay); <=0 falls back to the 2500 ms default. Never a measured duration and never used as run-proof.

measuredFrameMs is a Qt QTime::msecsTo() wall-clock delta between playback timer ticks; a non-positive value (clock stalled/went backwards) is excluded from the FPS EMA update rather than treated as proof a frame did or did not render.
Distinguishes the EMA's first sample (seed with the raw value) from a subsequent update (blend 90/10); the sentinel is an initialization marker, not run-proof.
Guards 1000.0 / m_playbackFpsEmaFrameMs (fps-from-frame-time) against a division by zero/uninitialized EMA before formatting the on-screen FPS label.

Chooses between the GPU-interop-measured wall_ms and a coarser texturePresentMs fallback when only the coarse timer produced a real reading; a display-value selection for the telemetry JSON, not a run-proof gate.

currentProcessCpuSeconds() returns -1.0 as an unavailable-clock sentinel; `lastCpuSeconds >= 0.0` gates the CPU-settle wait loop on that reading being available at all -- a feature-availability/data-validity decision (pairs with settleCpuPercent>=0.0 opting into the feature), never a stage run-proof.
Same CPU-settle availability decision as the loop guard above, computed once more into cpuSettleRequested for the diagnostic log line -- a config/data-validity read, not a stage run-proof.
notePhase3PlaybackTime() discards non-positive frame-time samples (and non-Phase-3 modes) before accumulating clip playtime; a sample-validity filter, not proof any stage ran.
flushPhase3PlaybackTime() has nothing to flush when the pending accumulator is empty or non-positive; an early-return guard on an accumulator, not a run-proof.

flushPhase3PlaybackTime rounds m_phase3ClipPlaytimePendingMs (a wall-clock accumulator, not a stage clock) down to whole seconds; when forced to flush early and truncation produced exactly 0, this substitutes a minimum-1-second fallback so a forced flush is never silently a no-op write. A fallback-value selection, not a run-proof.

Skips persisting the accumulated clip-playtime settings write when less than a second has accumulated and the flush was not forced -- an early-return threshold on a wall-clock accumulator, not proof that any pipeline stage ran.
Defensive clamp of the residual playtime accumulator to zero after subtracting the flushed whole seconds; guards integer-division residue, not run-proof.

Unit conversion (ms to s) for the playback-smoke summary log line; elapsedMs is derived from mlv_stage_timing_now() and the guard only avoids reporting a negative/garbage value, it does not decide whether anything ran.

Guards presentedFps = presentedFrames/elapsedSeconds and timelineFps = timelineDeltaAbs/elapsedSeconds in finishPlaybackSmokeTelemetry against dividing by zero when the smoke run's elapsed wall time (derived from mlv_stage_timing_now()) is non-positive; reports 0 fps instead. Formatting fallback for a diagnostic summary, never a run-proof.

Gates whether the playback_smoke.rbf_detail_summary diagnostic block is logged at all on whether the omp_get_wtime-direct RBF substage accumulator (processing_shadows_highlights_filter_rbf_total_ms, sourced from raw_processing.c's per-substage omp_get_wtime() writes ~1671-1694) summed to something nonzero across the session -- the named site from the #169 ruling (MainWindow.cpp smoke rbf_detail_summary ~25773).

Chooses between a measured render-thread-total-driven scope-update cadence and the configured base interval when the telemetry field read zero (not yet populated); a UI-update-interval selection, not a run-proof.
Part of the 'should I refresh the scopes now' throttle predicate (also true when never updated, or enough wall time elapsed); intervalMs is a UI cadence, not a stage-completion signal.

Excludes a non-positive inter-present interval (clock non-monotonic, or first frame) from being recorded into the playback-quality frame-time sampler; a sample-validity filter over a mlv_stage_timing_now()-derived interval (displayStart), not a run-proof.
tierEnteredAtMs is an epoch-ms sentinel meaning 'tier not yet entered' when <=0 (default-constructed); guards two promotion-eligibility checks, never a measured duration.
autoFallbackEpochMs is 0 when no auto-fallback has happened yet; the >0 check gates a 'still in cooldown after a recent auto-fallback' rule, not a duration/run-proof.
Standard fps-from-frame-time division guard; frameMs is a caller-supplied sample, not itself a run-proof signal.
recordFrameMs() drops non-positive samples before pushing into the sliding window; a sample-validity filter.

rows.anchor: if ( ! std :: isfinite ( ms ) || ms <= 0.0 ) return 0 ;
rows.justification: The durationNs() lambda clamps a millisecond duration to 0 before converting to nanoseconds (ms*1e6) for CSV event timestamps, guarding against a non-finite or negative value producing a nonsensical duration in the emitted event. A unit-conversion clamp, not itself the run-proof decision -- the actual run/skip decisions for these stages are the already-inventoried decodeMs<=0.0 (line 2958) and reconMs<=0.0 (line 2962) run_proof rows this same function computes just above.

Part of the Phase-3 CSV stage-timing emission named as a BLOCKER in the #169 review (RenderFrameThread.cpp ~2921-2966): a zero read from llrawproc_total_ms falls back to llrawproc_ms and, combined with the reconMs<=0.0 gate at line 2962, a genuinely-fast-but-real recon stage cannot be told apart from one that did not run at all; both readings trace to mlv_stage_timing_now()-based accumulators.

Same Phase-3 CSV fallback chain as the reconMs site (processed8_total_ms -> processed16_total_ms -> processing_ms); a zero read is treated as 'field not populated', indistinguishable from 'stage ran in under clock resolution'. Named in the #169 review BLOCKER for RenderFrameThread.cpp ~2921-2966.

Second link of the same processMs fallback chain (processed16_total_ms -> processing_ms); see the processed8_total_ms link's justification above. Named in the #169 review BLOCKER for RenderFrameThread.cpp ~2921-2966.

Suppresses emitting the MLV_STAGE_DECODE CSV event entirely when decodeMs read <=0.0 for a decode-only/decode-recon-process Phase-3 mode -- the named BLOCKER: a decode that legitimately completed in under clock resolution is indistinguishable from one that never ran, and the CSV consumer treats the missing event as 'did not run'.
Suppresses emitting the MLV_STAGE_RECON CSV event when reconMs read <=0.0 in DecodeReconProcess mode -- the other half of the sol/fable #169 BLOCKER named for this file (~2921-2966).

Reads llrawproc->playback_pre_dualiso_fix_ms > 0.0 as proof the pre-dual-ISO fix ran for THIS frame's telemetry dims. The field is a thread-local reset only at explicit reset points (llrawproc.c ~2825-2828) and written from mlv_stage_timing_now() at llrawproc.c ~3233, but the processed8 cache-hit path in getMlvProcessedFrame8_with_scale() (video_mlv.c, cache-hit branch ~7325-7364, reached via goto cleanup at ~7363) does NOT reset or replay it -- a cache-hit frame can report the calling thread's stale value from an earlier miss frame. This is the #169-review cache-hit-replay BLOCKER (video_mlv.c ~7334-7376 / entry reset ~7235-7247).

CLI arg range validation for the GUI-smoke harness's --seconds option (must be greater than 0), the same shape as the --settle-ms/--start-frame/--presented-frames checks immediately below it. Rejects malformed input before any run begins; cannot distinguish 'ran' from 'did not run'.
gui-smoke CLI argument range validation (--settle-ms must be >=0); a config-input check, unrelated to whether any playback stage ran.
gui-smoke CLI argument range validation (--settle-cpu-stable-ms must be >=0); a config-input check, unrelated to whether any playback stage ran.
gui-smoke CLI argument range validation (--stress-switch-at-ms must be >=0); a config-input check, unrelated to whether any playback stage ran.

durationFieldPlanned only includes the duration cross-check in the rendered-output verification plan when expectedDurationSeconds is a meaningful positive value (it is 0 when the source frame count wasn't ready) -- a verification-readiness/data-validity decision about what to check, not proof that rendering itself ran (that is frameCountFieldPlanned's job, ANDed in first).

frameCountExpectationReady requires both expectedFrameCount>0 and expectedDurationSeconds>0.0 before the frame-count check is considered plannable -- a verification-readiness decision derived from source metadata, not proof that any stage ran.

Parses ffmpeg's `out_time_us=` progress line (an external process's stderr, not an internal stage clock); only overwrites facts.durationSeconds when the parsed microsecond value is positive, so a malformed/absent progress line leaves the prior value untouched. A parsed-value acceptance filter, not a run-proof.

expectedDuration (framesToExport/frameRate, 0 when frameRate is unavailable) gates whether the decoded-vs-expected duration tolerance check runs at all; the frame-count check just above it is what actually guards exported content. A verification-readiness decision, not a stage run-proof.

dng_payload_writer_debug_delay() is an opt-in MLVAPP_* debug knob to artificially slow DNG writes for testing; delay_ms==0 (the default, unset) skips the sleep entirely. Not a measured duration and not run-proof.

First-frame sentinel: no prior frame finish has been recorded yet (initial value 0.0), so there is no queue-idle interval to compute. export_profile_now_ms() is QueryPerformanceCounter-based (Windows) / CLOCK_MONOTONIC elsewhere -- the same family as mlv_stage_timing_now().
Clamps a computed idle interval to zero when clock skew or reordering would otherwise produce a negative value; a defensive clamp on an optional export-profiler diagnostic, not a run-proof.
Producer-side counterpart of the frame-finish sentinel above: no prior producer finish recorded yet, so there is no producer-queue-idle interval to compute.
Producer-queue counterpart of the idle-interval clamp above.
export_profile_stage_set() clamps an externally-supplied stage duration to zero if negative before recording it into the optional export profiler; a defensive clamp, not a run-proof.

first_frame_with_raw_decode_telemetry()'s search for 'a frame that actually exercised raw decode' uses raw_uint16_ms > 0.0 as one of five OR'd signals (the others are the lj92 predictor field and three *_requested booleans); a raw decode that completed in under clock resolution would fail this leg of the OR silently (mitigated, not eliminated, by the other four signals). Named as the card's 'test_clip_golden.cpp frame selector (~227-245)' known debt.

Generic per-field schema check shared by many call sites in require_processing_timing_field(): any telemetry timing field must be a non-negative double. >=0.0 can never distinguish 'ran' from 'did not run' (both satisfy it), so it is never a run-proof, only a type/range sanity check.

Golden-JSON assertion that the whole-session average GUI frame latency measured nonzero; a real wall-clock GUI round-trip (Qt-timer based, not mlv_stage_timing_now), so not part of the omp_get_wtime 1 ms flake class, but still literally 'duration as proof a playback session produced measured frames' with no completed-flag alternative recorded alongside it.

Same class as average_latency_ms: a GUI round-trip wall-clock measurement asserted nonzero as proof the first frame was actually presented, with no completed-flag alternative. Occurs in three tests sharing this exact assertion line.
